instruction.text: Listen to each person by tapping on their picture and match the pieces of information accordingly.

cats.sound: ssml: <prosody volume = 'x-loud'>My partner and I are saving up to go backpacking in Thailand because we think it's the best way to have a holiday on a limited budget. The idea is to fly in cheap into Bangkok and then go island-hopping. We want to hike to epic viewpoints, snorkel in turquoise bays, crash in $15/night beach huts, and really experience nature. Not yet knowing where exactly we're going or doing gives us the perfect flexible and intimate adventure we wish for.</prosody>

As an older man, I find planning my travels very exhausting. That is why I'd love a two-week guided trip on a beautiful coast in Italy. I'm not as fit as I used to be, so a small group and expert guides for easy cliffside walks, comfy coach rides, well-prepared meals, and comfortable hotels suit me best. No planning hassles, just soaking in the history, culture, at a leisurely pace that suits my retirement perfectly.

For me, the best holiday would be a big all-inclusive week with my girls. After the monotony of work, we deserve a stay at a nice fancy beach hotel: the dream would be private overwater bungalows, endless gourmet meals, unlimited scuba dives and spa sessions, nightly shows, and so on. Total bliss—no leaving the resort, just sharing the luxury together with friends would be perfect.

atoms.sound: Backpacking is well suited for a low budget.
Thailand's nature can be experienced through hiking and swimming.
A looser holiday plan can provide flexibility and a sense of adventure.
A preplanned holiday is perfect for retirement.
Guided tours present easy access to experiencing history and culture.
A safe walking tour with experts is most suitable for someone with restricted mobility.
An all-in hotel will provide relaxation and recovery from work.
Sharing a trip with friends is part of a perfect holiday.
Having spa time and luxury helps to recover from the monotony of work life.
